references.text: Moses receives the two tablets of the testimony on Mount Sinai, written with God's finger.
Moses comes down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand.
God commands Moses to carve out two new stone tablets after the first ones were broken.
The continuation of the account about Moses' radiant face and how the Israelites reacted.
Moses recalls how he received the tablets of the covenant on the mountain after forty days and forty nights.
Moses tells about the new stone tablets that God wrote on, which were placed in the ark.
Paul refers directly to Moses' radiant face, which the Israelites could not look at, as a picture of the glory of the law.
Paul uses the veil that Moses placed over his face as an illustration of the difference between the old and the new covenant.
Complementary verses that together complete the theme of God's glory reflecting on humanity and requiring concealment.
A theological contrast showing continuity in God's communication: from the dangerous glory on the mountain to the structured presence in the tent of meeting.
